description: Idriss DÃ©by led the Patriotic Salvation Movement (MPS) from Sudan into Chad, capturing N'Djamena on December 1 and overthrowing HissÃ¨ne HabrÃ©'s eight-year dictatorship. DÃ©by suspended the constitution and established a transitional government under his presidency.

title: Movement for Democracy and Development Rebellion Begins
description: Armed opposition groups including the Movement for Democracy and Development launched rebellions in southern Chad against DÃ©by's new government. The insurrections reflected deep ethnic and regional tensions between the northern-dominated military regime and southern populations.

title: Sovereign National Conference Convened
description: DÃ©by convened a Sovereign National Conference with over 800 delegates to chart a democratic transition. The conference adopted a transitional charter, established a Higher Transitional Council, and set a timeline for multiparty elections.

title: CFA Franc Devaluation Doubles Import Costs
description: France devalued the CFA franc by 50% in January 1994, doubling the cost of imports for Chad and other Franc Zone countries. The devaluation triggered inflation and hardship for urban populations while boosting cotton export competitiveness over time.

title: New Constitution Approved by Referendum
description: Chadians approved a new constitution by referendum establishing a presidential republic with a two-term limit and multiparty system. The constitution was seen as a key step in the democratic transition begun at the 1993 national conference.

title: DÃ©by Wins First Multiparty Presidential Election
description: Idriss DÃ©by won Chad's first multiparty presidential election in a second-round runoff against General Wadal Abdelkader KamouguÃ©. International observers noted irregularities but the result was accepted, formalizing DÃ©by's transition from military ruler to elected president.

title: MDJT Rebellion Erupts in Tibesti Mountains
description: The Movement for Democracy and Justice in Chad (MDJT) launched an armed rebellion in the northern Tibesti region under former defense minister Youssouf TogoÃ¯mi. The insurgency tied down government forces in remote desert terrain for several years.

title: World Bank Approves Chad-Cameroon Pipeline Revenue Plan
description: The World Bank approved funding for the Chad-Cameroon petroleum development and pipeline project, with an unprecedented revenue management plan directing oil earnings to poverty reduction. The 1,070-km pipeline would connect Doba basin fields to a Cameroonian export terminal.

title: DÃ©by Re-elected in Disputed Second Term
description: DÃ©by won re-election with over 63% of the vote in a poll boycotted or contested by several opposition candidates. The opposition alleged widespread fraud, but DÃ©by consolidated power heading into the oil era.

title: Darfur Conflict Spills Over into Eastern Chad
description: The eruption of the Darfur conflict in neighboring Sudan sent over 200,000 refugees into eastern Chad and destabilized the border region. Janjaweed militias conducted cross-border raids into Chadian territory, straining government resources and inflaming ethnic tensions among shared Arab and non-Arab communities.

title: First Crude Oil Exported via Chad-Cameroon Pipeline
description: Chad began exporting oil through the newly completed Chad-Cameroon pipeline, transforming the country's fiscal position virtually overnight. Oil revenues quickly became the dominant source of government income, but management of the funds became a source of intense political controversy.

title: Failed Military Coup Attempt Against DÃ©by
description: Elements of the Chadian military attempted a coup against President DÃ©by in May 2004, reflecting growing discontent within the armed forces over ethnic favoritism and power concentration. DÃ©by survived and purged suspected plotters from the officer corps.

title: Constitutional Referendum Abolishes Presidential Term Limits
description: A constitutional referendum removed the two-term presidential limit, allowing DÃ©by to run indefinitely. The opposition boycotted the vote and denounced it as a constitutional coup, while international observers criticized the process.

title: Chad Breaks World Bank Oil Revenue Agreement
description: Chad's parliament amended the 1999 petroleum revenue management law, redirecting oil income away from the World Bank-supervised poverty reduction framework to general government spending including security. The World Bank suspended its lending program in response.

title: Rebels Attack N'Djamena â€” State of Emergency Declared
description: The United Front for Democratic Change (FUC) launched a major assault on N'Djamena in April 2006, reaching the presidential palace before being repelled by loyalist forces. DÃ©by declared a state of emergency and accused Sudan of backing the rebels.

title: DÃ©by Wins Third Term Amid Opposition Boycott
description: DÃ©by won a third presidential term with over 64% of the vote after the main opposition parties boycotted the election. The EU declined to send observers, citing insufficient conditions for credible elections.

title: Humanitarian Crisis Deepens in Eastern Chad
description: Ongoing Darfur spillover violence displaced over 180,000 Chadians internally while refugee camps housed 250,000 Sudanese. The UN authorized EUFOR Chad/CAR to protect civilians and humanitarian operations in eastern Chad and northeastern Central African Republic.

title: Second Major Rebel Assault on N'Djamena
description: A coalition of rebel groups launched a second large-scale attack on N'Djamena in February 2008, reaching the presidential palace compound before French military support helped government forces repel them. Hundreds of civilians were killed and tens of thousands fled the capital.

title: EUFOR Chad/CAR Peacekeeping Mission Deploys
description: The European Union Force Chad/CAR deployed 3,700 troops to eastern Chad and northeastern Central African Republic to protect refugees and displaced civilians from Darfur spillover violence. The mission marked Europe's largest autonomous military operation in Africa at the time.

title: MINURCAT Takes Over UN Peacekeeping in Eastern Chad
description: The UN Mission in the Central African Republic and Chad (MINURCAT) replaced EUFOR, deploying military and police to protect civilians in eastern Chad. The mission would be terminated in 2010 at Chad's request after relations with the government deteriorated.

title: Chad-Sudan Rapprochement Ends Proxy War
description: Chad and Sudan signed a normalization agreement and deployed joint border patrols, ending years of proxy warfare in which each country had backed rebel groups against the other. The rapprochement significantly reduced cross-border violence in the Darfur-Chad corridor.

title: DÃ©by Wins Fourth Term with 89% of Vote
description: DÃ©by won a fourth presidential term with nearly 89% of the vote after three main opposition candidates withdrew, citing irregularities. The election cemented the pattern of uncompetitive polls under DÃ©by's tenure.

title: Chad Deploys Troops to Mali Intervention
description: Chad contributed 2,000 troops to the French-led Operation Serval in northern Mali, becoming the largest African contributor. Chadian forces suffered significant casualties in the Adrar des Ifoghas mountains fighting Islamist militants.

title: Multinational Joint Task Force Reactivated Against Boko Haram
description: Chad played a leading role in reactivating the Multinational Joint Task Force to combat Boko Haram's expansion around the Lake Chad Basin. Chadian forces launched cross-border operations into Nigeria and Cameroon, positioning DÃ©by as a regional security guarantor.

title: Boko Haram Launches Suicide Bombings in N'Djamena
description: Boko Haram carried out its first suicide bombings in N'Djamena in June and July 2015, killing dozens and bringing the Lake Chad Basin conflict directly into the capital. Chad declared a state of emergency and banned the wearing of full-face veils.

title: Lake Chad Shrinks to Fraction of Historic Size
description: Lake Chad had shrunk by approximately 90% from its 1960s extent due to climate change, irrigation, and population growth, triggering a humanitarian crisis affecting over 10 million people across four countries. The ecological collapse destroyed fishing and farming livelihoods.

title: DÃ©by Wins Fifth Term â€” Opposition Leader Arrested
description: DÃ©by won a fifth presidential term with 59.5% of the vote. Prominent opposition candidate Saleh Kebzabo, who came second, rejected the results. Security forces cracked down on post-election protests.

title: Severe Austerity Amid Oil Price Collapse
description: Collapsed global oil prices since 2014 forced Chad into severe fiscal austerity, with public sector salary arrears and cuts to social services. The economic crisis provoked widespread strikes by civil servants, teachers, and healthcare workers throughout 2017-2018.

title: New Constitution Establishes Fourth Republic
description: Chad adopted a new constitution replacing the semi-presidential system with a presidential one, abolishing the prime minister position and concentrating executive power. The opposition denounced it as a constitutional power grab that further entrenched DÃ©by's authoritarian rule.

title: US Includes Chad in Travel Ban Then Reverses
description: The United States added Chad to its travel ban list in September 2017, citing information-sharing deficiencies, despite Chad being a key counterterrorism partner. The ban was lifted in April 2018 after Chad improved its passport security systems.

title: Boko Haram Kills 98 Chadian Soldiers at Bohoma
description: A Boko Haram attack on the military base at Bohoma in the Lac Province killed 98 Chadian soldiers in March 2020, the deadliest single incident for Chad's military. DÃ©by personally traveled to the region and launched Operation Wrath of Bohoma in retaliation.

title: FACT Rebel Column Invades from Southern Libya
description: The Front for Change and Concord in Chad (FACT) launched a major armed incursion from southern Libya in April 2021, advancing hundreds of kilometers toward N'Djamena. The rebel offensive was the direct cause of President DÃ©by's death on the frontline.

title: COVID-19 Compounds Humanitarian Crisis
description: Chad imposed a state of health emergency and border closures in response to COVID-19, compounding existing food insecurity and displacement crises. The pandemic disrupted humanitarian access to the 700,000+ refugees and internally displaced persons.

title: France Launches Operation Barkhane Strike from Chad
description: France used its major military base in N'Djamena as a hub for Operation Barkhane counterterrorism operations across the Sahel. Chad hosted over 1,000 French troops, making it central to France's military architecture in Africa.

title: DÃ©by Killed on Frontline â€” Transitional Military Council Formed
description: President Idriss DÃ©by was killed on April 20, 2021, from wounds sustained while visiting troops fighting FACT rebels in northern Chad, one day after being declared winner of a sixth presidential term. His son Mahamat Idriss DÃ©by took power as head of a Transitional Military Council, dissolving parliament and the constitution.

title: Security Forces Kill Protesters Opposing Military Takeover
description: Security forces killed at least 13 people during protests against the Transitional Military Council's seizure of power in April and May 2021. Opposition groups and civil society condemned the dynastic succession as an unconstitutional coup.

title: African Union and France Endorse Transitional Council
description: The African Union and France gave de facto support to the Transitional Military Council despite its unconstitutional nature, citing Chad's strategic importance for Sahel counterterrorism. The AU called for an 18-month transition to civilian rule.

title: Deadly Crackdown on Pro-Democracy Protests â€” Black Thursday
description: Security forces killed at least 50 people and injured hundreds during protests on October 20, 2022, against the military council's decision to extend the transition period by two years. The day became known as Black Thursday and drew international condemnation.

title: National Dialogue Boycotted by Key Opposition Groups
description: The Transitional Military Council held an inclusive national dialogue, but major opposition parties and rebel groups including FACT boycotted it. The dialogue concluded by extending the transition by two years and allowing Mahamat DÃ©by to run in future elections.

title: France Begins Barkhane Withdrawal â€” Sahel Realignment
description: France announced the end of Operation Barkhane and began reconfiguring its military presence in the Sahel, while maintaining its base in N'Djamena. The withdrawal from Mali and reduced regional footprint raised questions about Chad's future role as a French security partner.

title: New Constitution Approved â€” Fifth Republic Established
description: A constitutional referendum approved a new text establishing Chad's Fifth Republic, replacing the unitary state with a nominally decentralized system. Opposition groups denounced the process as engineered to legitimize the military transition.

title: Wagner Group Influence Expands in Neighboring States
description: Russia's Wagner Group expanded its presence in neighboring Central African Republic and Sudan, raising concerns about potential destabilization of Chad's borders. Chad navigated between maintaining French security ties and managing growing Russian influence in the region.

title: Lake Chad Basin Displacement Exceeds 3 Million
description: Conflict, climate change, and food insecurity drove displacement in the Lake Chad Basin to over 3 million people across four countries. Chad hosted over 600,000 Sudanese refugees in addition to hundreds of thousands of internally displaced persons.

title: Mahamat DÃ©by Wins Presidential Election with 61%
description: Mahamat Idriss DÃ©by won the May 2024 presidential election with 61% of the vote, completing the transition from military to civilian rule. His main rival, Prime Minister SuccÃ¨s Masra, initially rejected the results before eventually accepting them.

title: Chad Terminates Defense Cooperation Agreement with France
description: Chad abruptly terminated its defense cooperation agreement with France in November 2024, ordering the withdrawal of French troops from Chadian territory. The move ended decades of French military presence and reflected a broader trend of declining French influence across the Sahel.

title: Sudanese Civil War Drives Massive Refugee Influx
description: The civil war in Sudan that began in April 2023 drove over 700,000 additional refugees into eastern Chad by late 2024, overwhelming humanitarian capacity. Chad became the world's largest refugee host relative to its resources and GDP.

title: Chad Pivots Toward Russia and Turkey for Security
description: Following the termination of the French defense pact, Chad began diversifying its security partnerships, engaging with Russia, Turkey, and Gulf states. The pivot marked a fundamental shift in Chad's postcolonial foreign policy orientation.

title: French Military Withdrawal from N'Djamena Completed
description: France completed the withdrawal of its remaining troops from Chad in early 2025, ending over six decades of continuous French military presence. The departure closed the last major French base in the Sahel region.

title: Escalating Sahel Instability Threatens Chad's Borders
description: Continued instability in Sudan, Libya, and the Central African Republic created a ring of conflict around Chad, straining its security forces across multiple fronts. Jihadist activity in the Lake Chad Basin persisted despite military operations.
